title: Connect Claude Code to WordPress with MCP (Then Lock It Down)

notes.tone: Friendly, practical British how-to with a bit of edge: a setup walkthrough that keeps coming back to 'lock it down'. Talking head carries the personality, the stories and the key points; the screen carries the clicks and the code. Light, unobtrusive music bed under the talking head and screen sections, dropped out for the SSH story in the guard rails section. Burnt-in captions throughout (lots of code terms: spell them exactly as the script does, in monospace where they are code). Recurring graphics: numbered chapter cards '1.' to '5.' for the five steps, one consistent style; the illustrated kitchen (hatch, cupboard, jars, padlocks, the .mcp.json key) introduced in the analogy section and brought back in the Shop Manager test, the SSH story and the ability walkthrough, so build it once as a reusable layered illustration. Callouts and lower thirds use the same clean card style. On-screen text uses British English and no em dashes. Screen recordings at a readable zoom (editor font large, browser at 125% or more), cursor highlighted. Nothing sensitive on screen unblurred: see blur_list.
notes.before_timeline: 1) SSH claim: the cold open and the guard rails section both depend on the real terminal transcript of Claude reaching for SSH (b01.mg1, b36.sr1). Get the actual transcript before editing; if it can't be found, the claim needs rethinking, not a mock-up presented as real. 2) Shop Manager test (b33): the script's own fact check asks to confirm the order answers came through MCP abilities and not another route. Make sure the recording shows the MCP tool call in the Claude Code output. 3) 'Nothing of our own in the cupboard' (sentence 102): run discover-abilities before the edit so the line matches what the site actually exposes. 4) MCP Adapter release: the script names a ready-made mcp-adapter.zip on the Releases page (v0.6.1, 13 August 2026 at time of writing); check it is still the latest on the day. 'Being assessed for the plugin directory' (sentence 27) is hedged as hearsay; link a source in the description if there is one. 5) Screen cue for step three says 'GitHub ... then terminal', but the step now downloads the release zip rather than cloning and building, so there is no terminal in this step; b09/b10 follow the zip route. Confirm nothing terminal-based is needed. 6) Sentence 49 says copy the object from the docs, but the cue for sentences 50 to 61 says type each line as it's described. Decide which is shown: suggested approach is paste the docs object, then build it up line by line with each key highlighted as it's mentioned (b18 to b25). 7) The 'finished .mcp.json with ${} variables' screen (b23) comes before LOG_FILE is described (b25). Either show the file without LOG_FILE at b23 and add it in b25, or accept the line is already there and just highlight it in b25. 8) ${VAR} expansion in .mcp.json only works if the variables are set in the shell that launches Claude Code; the script's fact check asks for a one-line on-screen mention (added as b23.callout1). 9) The deny rules in b38: check the exact permission syntax against the current Claude Code settings docs before recording the screen. 10) The script never names the create ability (only casagees/get-order-slots); on-screen text in b53 says 'create order slots' rather than inventing a name. 11) Audience brief says the ability build (sec11 and sec12) is optional detail and could be split into its own video. This paper edit keeps it; if it's cut, beats b44 to b58 go and the end screen follows b43. 12) Chapters follow the script's metadata list, plus one added chapter 'How the ability works' at b44 so the code walkthrough is findable; drop it if you want the description to match the metadata exactly.

notes.structure: Hook (SSH tease) and problem in sec01, five numbered steps with the kitchen analogy between steps three and four, a quick role test, then the SSH payoff and guard rails, then the real-world ability. Keep the steps brisk and the analogy and guard rails slower; they are the bits nobody else covers.
notes.end_screen: Last beat (b59) is talking head framed left with end screen elements on the right for the last 20 seconds; est_seconds is set to 20 so the picture holds if the speech runs short.

sections.purpose: Cold open. Tease the SSH story in the first ten seconds, then set up the problem: official docs exist but skip the setup and the config file. Quick, confident, on camera; define MCP in one breath.
Step one: a dedicated user with the lowest role. Screen-led and brisk, landing on camera for why you never hand an AI your admin account.
Step two: the application password. Screen-led; blur the password. Ends on camera with the 'they just sit there' beat.
Step three: install the MCP Adapter from the GitHub release. Screen-led, then the three greyed-out icons set up the analogy.
The insight. The kitchen analogy: hatch (MCP server), jars (abilities), padlocks (permissions), key (the local .mcp.json). Slower, warmer, on camera with the illustration building as the lines land.
Step four: build .mcp.json line by line. The core of what viewers came for. Clear, methodical screen work, with a hold on the finished file so people can pause and copy it.
Step five: start Claude Code, approve the server, prove it's connected, recap the checklist. Small payoff moment.
Show that the role changes what the AI can see (Shop Manager test), then put it straight back. Quick and honest.
The SSH payoff and the guard rails. Serious for a moment, on camera for the story, then CLAUDE.md and settings deny rules. Belt and braces.
The real-world reason to build an ability: CasaGees delivery slots that need regenerating every week. Personal, on camera, with the calendar graphics.
Confession that AI built the ability, then a walk through the main plugin file: category (the shelf) and the permission callback (the padlock).
Inside the ability: registration, execute and permission callbacks, input and output schema, and the mcp public flag. Screen-led with one on-camera summary of what the Abilities API is really for.
End screen. Point to the theory video, one call to action, sign off.
